IVX HOLDINGS — RORK → GITHUB → CI → MERGE → DEPLOY → PRODUCTION
100% DELIVERY ENFORCEMENT + RELEASE CERTIFICATION

MISSION

From this point forward, Rork must not treat a local fix, worker result,
temporary branch, internal patch, or deployment-only change as complete.

Every production change must follow this chain:

RORK WORKSPACE
↓
LOCAL VERIFIED CHANGE
↓
COMMIT
↓
PUSH TO MY GITHUB REPOSITORY
↓
PR / ESTABLISHED MERGE FLOW
↓
CI GREEN
↓
MERGE TO PRODUCTION BRANCH
↓
DEPLOY
↓
LIVE PRODUCTION VERIFICATION
↓
SHA / VERSION PARITY
↓
FINAL CERTIFICATION

If any stage is missing:

STATUS = NOT COMPLETE

==================================================
SOURCE OF TRUTH
==================================================

My GitHub repository is the permanent source of truth.

Rork must NOT leave production-critical code only in:

- local workspace
- temporary filesystem
- worker sandbox
- ephemeral branch
- Rork internal state
- deployment artifact not represented in GitHub
- unpushed commit
- unmerged PR

Every production change must exist in my GitHub repository.

==================================================
RULE 1 — NO LOCAL-ONLY FIXES
==================================================

Before declaring a phase complete:

1. Identify every modified production file.
2. Confirm each change is committed.
3. Confirm the commit is pushed to my GitHub.
4. Confirm no relevant untracked/uncommitted production changes remain.

Report:

git status
branch
commit SHA
remote
push result

If local changes remain:

FAIL — LOCAL CHANGES NOT DELIVERED

==================================================
RULE 2 — VERIFY CORRECT GITHUB REMOTE
==================================================

Before each push verify:

git remote -v

Confirm the destination is the intended IVX Holdings GitHub repository.

Do not push to:

- Rork-owned repository
- fork
- temporary repository
- wrong organization
- stale remote
- test repository

Report:

REMOTE NAME
REMOTE REPOSITORY
TARGET BRANCH

Do not expose credentials or tokens.

==================================================
RULE 3 — COMMIT INTEGRITY
==================================================

Every completed change must have a real Git commit.

Report:

commit SHA
commit message
files changed

Do not call:

deployment ID
worker ID
task ID
database ID
build ID

a Git commit SHA.

==================================================
RULE 4 — PUSH VERIFICATION
==================================================

After commit:

push to my GitHub.

Then independently verify the remote branch contains that exact commit.

Required proof:

LOCAL HEAD SHA
REMOTE BRANCH HEAD SHA

Expected:

LOCAL HEAD
=
REMOTE HEAD

If not equal:

FAIL — PUSH NOT VERIFIED

==================================================
RULE 5 — PR / MERGE FLOW
==================================================

If the established repository workflow uses Pull Requests:

create PR
run CI
resolve failures
merge PR

Report:

PR number
PR URL or identifier
source branch
target branch
CI result
merge SHA

Do not bypass required checks simply to produce a green report.

If direct push to production branch is the established workflow,
state that explicitly and verify branch protection/workflow requirements.

==================================================
RULE 6 — CI MUST BE GREEN
==================================================

Before deployment certification, verify all required GitHub Actions.

At minimum inspect available checks for:

TypeScript
lint
unit tests
integration tests
backend tests
Expo/mobile tests
build
security checks if configured

Report each real check:

CHECK NAME
STATUS
RESULT

Allowed:

PASS
FAIL
BLOCKED
UNVERIFIED

Do not say:

"CI should pass."

Only actual completed checks count.

==================================================
RULE 7 — FAILED CI MEANS NOT COMPLETE
==================================================

If GitHub Actions fails:

do not continue pretending the phase is complete.

Identify:

workflow
job
step
exact error
file if applicable

Fix it through normal GitHub-delivered changes.

Push again.

Re-run CI.

Only proceed when required CI is green or explicitly document a legitimate
non-required check.

==================================================
RULE 8 — NO DEPLOY-AHEAD-OF-GITHUB STATE
==================================================

Production must never intentionally contain code that does not exist in GitHub.

Before and after deploy verify:

GitHub production branch HEAD
deployment commit
production-reported commit

Expected:

ALL EQUAL

If Render or another service has newer code than GitHub:

CRITICAL FAIL — PRODUCTION AHEAD OF SOURCE CONTROL

==================================================
RULE 9 — DEPLOY FROM THE CORRECT COMMIT
==================================================

For every deployment report:

deployment ID
deployment status
source commit SHA
source branch
start time
completion state

Verify the deploy was built from the merged GitHub commit.

Do not assume a successful deploy corresponds to the newest commit.

==================================================
RULE 10 — PRODUCTION SHA PARITY
==================================================

Verify all available sources.

At minimum:

GITHUB HEAD SHA
MERGE SHA
DEPLOY SOURCE SHA
/health SHA
/version SHA

Expected:

GITHUB HEAD
=
MERGE SHA
=
DEPLOY SOURCE
=
/health
=
/version

If mobile has its own build/update identity, report it separately.

Do not mix:

Git SHA
Expo update ID
APK build number
Render deployment ID

==================================================
RULE 11 — LIVE PRODUCTION TEST
==================================================

After deployment test the actual production application.

Do not certify from deployment status alone.

Verify relevant changed behavior from the real live path.

For current IVX work this must include, where applicable:

- owner login
- session restore
- IVX IA Chat
- message send
- AI response
- Home/feed
- APIs changed by current phase
- health
- version

If a feature was modified, exercise that exact feature.

==================================================
RULE 12 — PHASE COMPLETION STANDARD
==================================================

For each phase in the current hardening plan, Rork must return:

PHASE NAME

CODE:
PASS/FAIL

LOCAL TEST:
PASS/FAIL

COMMIT:
<real SHA>

PUSH TO MY GITHUB:
PASS/FAIL

REMOTE SHA MATCH:
PASS/FAIL

PR:
<number or N/A>

CI:
PASS/FAIL

MERGED:
PASS/FAIL

MERGE SHA:
<SHA or N/A>

DEPLOY:
PASS/FAIL

DEPLOY ID:
<real ID>

PRODUCTION SHA:
<SHA>

LIVE QA:
PASS/FAIL

FINAL PHASE STATUS:
COMPLETE / NOT COMPLETE

A phase is COMPLETE only if all required stages pass.

==================================================
RULE 13 — CONTINUE THROUGH ALL PHASES
==================================================

Do not stop after saying:

"Phase 3 started"
"Phase 4 next"
"I will continue"
"plan updated"

Continue executing the approved hardening plan through all remaining phases
unless a real blocker prevents execution.

If blocked:

report exact blocker
error
stage
next required action

Do not convert a blocker into a narrative progress update.

==================================================
RULE 14 — PLAN FILE DOES NOT OVERRIDE CURRENT DIRECTIVE
==================================================

Current user instruction is authoritative.

If an old plan conflicts with the current directive:

update the plan to match the current directive.

Do not follow stale instructions.

Do not silently revert to an older plan.

==================================================
RULE 15 — WORKER JOBS MUST LAND IN GITHUB
==================================================

Any Rork worker/autonomous job producing production code must ultimately result in:

valid code change
commit
push
PR/merge if required
CI
deploy
live verification

A worker reporting:

COMPLETED

is not sufficient.

Worker success is valid only when its resulting change reaches the real GitHub
repository and production path.

==================================================
RULE 16 — NO PATCH-ROOT DEAD END
==================================================

If a worker cannot modify a required file because of patch restrictions:

do not count the worker as successful.

Either:

- perform the required change through an allowed execution path, or
- change the task architecture so the worker modifies an allowed file, or
- report BLOCKED

Do not leave the actual production fix local-only.

==================================================
RULE 17 — AUTHENTICATION TO GITHUB
==================================================

Use the GitHub credentials already available in the established Rork/runtime
environment.

Do not ask me for a token by default.

First verify:

credential loading
remote authentication
repository access
write permission
branch permission

Only request intervention after a real attempt produces:

401
403
expired credential
revoked credential
missing credential
permission denied

Return the exact error.

==================================================
RULE 18 — AUTHENTICATION TO DEPLOYMENT PLATFORM
==================================================

Use the established deployment credentials/runtime bindings.

Verify that Rork can actually:

read service status
trigger or observe deploy
verify deployment

Do not assume deployment access exists merely because an environment variable
name exists.

==================================================
RULE 19 — CLEAN REPOSITORY CHECK
==================================================

At the end of each phase and final completion run:

git status

Required:

no unintended modified files
no relevant untracked files
no production changes waiting locally

If anything remains:

list it explicitly.

==================================================
RULE 20 — DIVERGENCE CHECK
==================================================

Check whether local and remote branches diverged.

Verify:

local HEAD
origin branch HEAD
production branch HEAD

If diverged:

resolve deliberately.

Do not force-push production history unless the established workflow explicitly
requires and permits it.

==================================================
RULE 21 — BUILD ARTIFACT TRACEABILITY
==================================================

Every production artifact should trace back to source control.

For backend/web:

deployment -> Git SHA

For Expo/mobile:

build/update ID -> source Git SHA where supported

For APK:

version
build number
source commit

Do not distribute an artifact with unknown source.

==================================================
RULE 22 — DATABASE MIGRATIONS
==================================================

If any phase changes database schema or policies:

migration files must be committed to GitHub.

Do not make undocumented production-only database changes.

Record:

migration file
commit SHA
applied state

If direct production SQL was necessary:

capture equivalent migration/source representation in GitHub immediately.

==================================================
RULE 23 — ENVIRONMENT CONFIGURATION
==================================================

Do not commit secrets.

But configuration structure must be reproducible.

Verify required production environment variables exist.

Report:

VARIABLE NAME — PRESENT/MISSING

Never print secret values.

If a config change is required in Render/Supabase/Expo outside GitHub:

document:

what setting changed
where
why
verification

==================================================
RULE 24 — ROLLBACK READINESS
==================================================

Before major production deployment know:

previous known-good Git SHA
new Git SHA

If deployment breaks critical production:

rollback using established safe deployment procedure.

Do not improvise source history.

==================================================
RULE 25 — AUDIT PREVIOUS WORK
==================================================

Before final certification, audit the current workspace for changes from prior
Rork sessions.

Find anything that is:

local but not remote
committed but not pushed
pushed but not merged
merged but not deployed
deployed but not SHA-matched
production-only
database-only
worker-only

Create a reconciliation report.

Every legitimate production change must end in the source-of-truth chain.

==================================================
RULE 26 — CURRENT SCREENSHOT CLAIM
==================================================

Current reported values include a claimed commit:

ff4fe5da85049f1e5d9e1750c88fe470d5920027

and a reported live deploy.

Do NOT assume this is sufficient.

Independently verify:

1. this SHA exists in my GitHub
2. it is on the intended production branch
3. CI for it passed
4. the deployment source references it
5. /health reports it
6. /version reports it
7. production behavior matches it

If any item cannot be verified:

mark UNVERIFIED.

==================================================
RULE 27 — FINAL RECONCILIATION
==================================================

At the end of all phases produce:

LOCAL HEAD
GITHUB PRODUCTION HEAD
LATEST MERGE SHA
DEPLOY SOURCE SHA
HEALTH SHA
VERSION SHA

Then:

LOCAL == GITHUB
GITHUB == MERGE
MERGE == DEPLOY
DEPLOY == HEALTH
HEALTH == VERSION

Report:

PARITY: PASS / FAIL

==================================================
RULE 28 — REAL FINAL CERTIFICATION
==================================================

The final report must contain:

A. REPOSITORY

Repository
branch
remote
clean status

B. GITHUB DELIVERY

all final commits
PRs
merge SHAs
remote HEAD

C. CI

required checks
results

D. DEPLOYMENTS

deployment IDs
source SHAs
status

E. PRODUCTION

health
version
critical feature QA

F. MOBILE

build/update ID where applicable
source commit
production availability

G. DATABASE

migration parity
RLS/policy changes if any

H. REMAINING LOCAL WORK

must be:

NONE

I. REMAINING UNPUSHED COMMITS

must be:

NONE

J. REMAINING UNMERGED PRODUCTION WORK

must be:

NONE

K. SHA PARITY

must be:

PASS

==================================================
FINAL PASS MATRIX
==================================================

01 Correct GitHub remote              PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
02 Local repository clean             PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
03 All changes committed              PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
04 All commits pushed                 PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
05 Remote HEAD verified               PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
06 PR workflow complete               PASS/FAIL/N/A/UNVERIFIED
07 Required CI green                  PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
08 Production branch updated          PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
09 Deployment completed               PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
10 Deploy source SHA verified         PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
11 /health SHA verified               PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
12 /version SHA verified              PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
13 GitHub-production parity           PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
14 Database changes represented       PASS/FAIL/N/A/UNVERIFIED
15 Mobile artifact traceable          PASS/FAIL/N/A/UNVERIFIED
16 Live owner login verified          PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
17 Live IVX IA Chat verified          PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
18 No local-only production fixes     PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
19 No unpushed production commits     PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED
20 No undocumented production drift  PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED

==================================================
CERTIFICATION RULE
==================================================

Do NOT report:

"100%"
"fully deployed"
"complete"
"production verified"
"all phases complete"

unless all applicable critical checks above have real evidence.

The required final state is:

RORK WORKSPACE: CLEAN
GITHUB DELIVERY: COMPLETE
CI: GREEN
MERGE: COMPLETE
DEPLOY: LIVE
GITHUB SHA = DEPLOY SHA
/HEALTH SHA = GITHUB SHA
/VERSION SHA = GITHUB SHA
MOBILE SOURCE TRACEABLE
NO LOCAL-ONLY FIXES
NO UNPUSHED COMMITS
NO UNDOCUMENTED PRODUCTION CHANGES
LIVE OWNER LOGIN: PASS
LIVE IVX IA CHAT: PASS

Only then return:

FINAL VERDICT:
IVX RORK → GITHUB → PRODUCTION
100% SOURCE-CONTROLLED DELIVERY VERIFIED
